rv.q: Stella Powell-Jones' production doesn't always help a fusty script: touching when speakers gaze out, unsure how a letter will be received, but strenuous when she has the actors declaim at each other.
Even if you're unaware of the playwright and his muse this is still essential theatre, and despite their faults it's all but impossible not to fall for both of these astonishing individuals.
As a script, DEAR LIAR doesn't do justice to its central characters, but the Theatre's strong production enhances Kilty's play through strong performances and smart directing choices.
Powell-Jones and her team make the strongest possible case. A must-see for all lovers of theatre, wit, and wincing put-downs.
This play is beautifully crafted by Stella Powell-Jones with edge, wit and precision.
Pickup feels perfectly cast as Campbell, capturing her fire and charisma.

cn.t: This epistolary adaptation of Shaw and Mrs. Patrick Campbell's witty correspondence charms critics with its fascinating insight into their complex relationship, though some find the format lacks dramatic urgency.
